title: The Great Roll and the Witnesses
summary: Nephi reports the Lord’s instruction to take a great roll and write in it concerning Maher-shalal-hash-baz. Nephi reports taking Uriah the priest and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah as faithful witnesses to record.

explicit_facts.text: The word of the Lord tells the narrator, Nephi, to take a great roll and write in it with a man’s pen concerning Maher-shalal-hash-baz.
Nephi took Uriah the priest and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah as faithful witnesses to record.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A static retrospective illustration may represent Nephi and the two witnesses without depicting recording or placing them at the earlier instruction.
unspecified_visual_details: The location and everyone’s appearance are unspecified.
The roll’s material and dimensions and the pen’s appearance are unspecified.
How the word of the Lord was conveyed is unspecified.
The interval between the instruction and Nephi’s taking of witnesses is unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Take thee a great roll, and write in it with a man’s pen, concerning Maher-shalal-hash-baz.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

narration.text: And I took unto me faithful witnesses to record, Uriah the priest, and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Nephi is the first-person narrator.
The Lord’s dialogue is reported speech, not evidence of a visible divine appearance.
The instruction and the taking of witnesses are distinct reported events.
The text does not specify what the witnesses record or say that they perform any recording.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord visibly or invent a means of communication.
Do not show the commanded writing underway or completed.
Do not stage the reported events as new present-tense action or place the witnesses at the instruction.
Do not depict Maher-shalal-hash-baz or Jeberechiah as present.
Do not assert that the witnesses record writing on the roll.

title: The Child Is Named
summary: Nephi reports going to the prophetess, who conceived and bore a son. The Lord tells Nephi to name the child Maher-shalal-hash-baz and prophesies what will happen before the child knows how to cry for his father and mother.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi reports going to the prophetess, who conceived and bore a son.
The Lord tells Nephi to name the child Maher-shalal-hash-baz.
The Lord says that the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria shall be taken away before the king of Assyria before the child knows how to cry for his father and mother.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi may be shown listening to the Lord's words, with no visible depiction of the Lord.
The earlier events may be conveyed through narration rather than staged as present action.
unspecified_visual_details: Nephi's appearance and clothing
The setting of the Lord's instruction
Whether the prophetess and child are present during the instruction

spoken_dialogue.text: For behold, the child shall not have knowledge to cry, My father, and my mother, before the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria shall be taken away before the king of Assyria.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

narration.text: And I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived and bare a son.
Then said the Lord to me:

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The visit, conception, and birth are reported events preceding the Lord's instruction; do not combine them into one moment.
The taking of riches and spoil is a prophecy, not an event occurring in this scene.
My father, and my mother is part of the Lord's speech, not dialogue spoken by the child.
prohibited_inventions: Do not give the Lord a visible appearance.
Do not stage the reported visit, conception, or birth as present-tense action.
Do not depict the predicted taking of riches and spoil.
Do not invent additional dialogue, the prophetess's name, or a parental relationship for Nephi.
Do not place the king of Assyria physically in the scene.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord speaks again to Nephi.

narration.text: The Lord spake also unto me again, saying:

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The people’s refusal and rejoicing are reported in the Lord’s speech, not narrated as events occurring during the exchange.

title: Prophecy Concerning Assyria and Judah
summary: The prophecy identifies the rising river waters with the king of Assyria and his glory, foretells his passage through Judah and overflow reaching to the neck, and declares that the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of Immanuel’s land.

explicit_facts.text: The prophecy says the Lord brings up the river waters, identified as the king of Assyria and all his glory.
He shall come up over all his channels and go over all his banks.
He shall pass through Judah, overflow, and reach even to the neck.
The prophecy addresses Immanuel and says the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of Immanuel’s land.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The prophecy can be presented as text without staging its foretold events.
unspecified_visual_details: Typography and background are unspecified.
No present setting, visible participants, or physical appearance of wings is described.

narration.text: the Lord bringeth up upon them the waters of the river, strong and many, even the king of Assyria and all his glory;
And he shall pass through Judah; he shall overflow and go over, he shall reach even to the neck; and the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of thy land, O Immanuel.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is prophecy, not an advance occurring in the present scene.
The river waters are explicitly identified with the king of Assyria and his glory; do not stage a literal flood.
Preserve the statement about the stretching out of his wings without resolving its physical form or presenting it as a witnessed appearance.
Addressing Immanuel does not establish his visible presence.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage the foretold advance as a present event.
Do not invent a literal flood or a visible winged figure.
Do not depict the Lord or Immanuel as visibly present.
Do not invent a present setting, participants, dialogue, or appearances.

title: Counsel That Will Not Stand
summary: The verses address people and those of far countries, warn that they will be broken in pieces, and say that their counsel and word will not stand.

explicit_facts.text: The address calls on people to associate and those of far countries to give ear.
It repeatedly warns that those addressed will be broken in pieces.
It says counsel will come to naught and a spoken word will not stand, for God is with us.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The words can be presented without depicting a speaker, the people addressed, or the predicted outcomes.
unspecified_visual_details: Any speaker's identity or appearance

Take counsel together, and it shall come to naught; speak the word, and it shall not stand; for God is with us.

title: Do Not Fear Their Fear
summary: The Lord speaks to Nephi with a strong hand and instructs him not to walk in the way of this people. The Lord tells him not to say “A confederacy” as the people do or fear their fear, and to sanctify the Lord of Hosts.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord speaks to Nephi with a strong hand and instructs him not to walk in the way of this people.
The Lord says not to repeat the people's declaration of a confederacy or fear their fear.
The Lord says to sanctify the Lord of Hosts and let him be their fear and dread.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The Lord's words can be conveyed without showing a physical appearance.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting and Nephi's appearance.

title: Sanctuary and Stumbling Stone
summary: The passage foretells that he shall be a sanctuary, but also a stumbling stone and snare; many shall stumble, fall, be broken, be snared, and be taken.

explicit_facts.text: He shall be a sanctuary, but a stone of stumbling and rock of offense to both houses of Israel, and a gin and snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
Many among them shall stumble, fall, be broken, be snared, and be taken.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The contrasting images of sanctuary, stone, rock, and snare may be presented as figurative teaching rather than visible events.
unspecified_visual_details: The identity and appearance of the person called “he.”

narration.text: And he shall be for a sanctuary; but for a stone of stumbling, and for a rock of offense to both the houses of Israel, for a gin and a snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses foretell outcomes; they do not narrate those outcomes occurring in a visible scene.

title: To the Law and the Testimony
summary: The passage anticipates advice to seek those with familiar spirits and wizards, asks whether a people should seek their God, and directs attention to the law and testimony.

explicit_facts.text: The passage anticipates that unspecified people will tell others to seek those with familiar spirits and wizards who peep and mutter.
It asks whether a people should seek their God for the living to hear from the dead.
It invokes the law and the testimony and says that those who do not speak according to this word have no light in them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Present the teaching as text rather than staging the anticipated advice as an event.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, the identities and appearances of those addressed, and the visual design of any displayed text.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The advice is conditional, not an event narrated as occurring. Hearing from the dead is raised in a question, not described as an encounter. These verses do not identify a speaker of the teaching.
